parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminal offence is documented; same-sex conduct is legal, marriage equality arrived via a 2024 supreme-court ruling, and the criminal code prohibits orientation-based discrimination and incitement. Community infrastructure (LGBT centre since 2010), a gay-friendly reputation and functioning courts are documented positives. No universal-exposure measure, police targeting, custody rule or violence pattern appears anywhere in the record. Countervailing: gender identity is not a named protected ground, so a visitor denied service has no identified statutory remedy (thin, not active hostility); public LGBT assembly can be obstructed by last-minute permitting, showing administrative friction; trans-specific axes — border screening, facilities, care — are explicitly unassessed, which are open questions, not exposures. Absence of documented incidents in a small, well-documented island signals mild positives, but trans-specific acceptance itself is undocumented. Net: reduced risk with friction and thin recourse.
